_doc: The anchor registry. One name for one control, whichever surface it is on.
ATTRIBUTE: data-coach. NOT health_learn's data-a — Payobook already had 40+
live data-coach anchors across six modules before this module existed, and
renaming them would churn every template for zero behaviour. The engine
reads one constant (engine/spotlight.js).
KINDS
product   the control exists in a real product template; data-coach="key"
must be found there verbatim. `screen` may be a LIST when one
template serves several screens (pb_payrun_ledgers renders Full
& Final, Proration and Retro from one file) — `shared: true`
marks that, so nobody reads a single-screen promise into it.
pattern   the control exists once PER RECORD. The template emits the key
with t-attf-data-coach, so the registry declares the prefix and
the test looks for that prefix rather than a literal key. Empty
in Phase A on purpose — see pk-card.
reserved  a PRODUCT anchor no content points at YET. Phase C1 anchored
whole regions of seven cockpits in one pass, because the
alternative is a second edit to somebody else's template for
every lesson written afterwards — and each of those is a chance
for a tidy-up to delete an attribute nothing over there reads.
THE RULE: an anchor may be laid ahead of its content where the
region is certain to be taught, and the registry says so with
`reserved: true`. It is a claim with a cost — the anchor is
still checked against its template on every run — and the flag
comes OFF the moment content names it, which test_08 enforces in
both directions. An anchor that is neither referenced nor
reserved is a typo or a leftover.
practice  a TEACHING view with no product counterpart: an arithmetic
breakdown, a lifecycle stepper, the replica's own navigation.
Named rep-* and declared so the gap is VISIBLE — the Coach must
never claim to point at one of these on a live screen.
foreign   data-coach anchors this module does not own. They belong to
pb_formula_studio, to pb_hr_payroll_formula and to PayAI, they
predate pb_learn, and they are listed so the lint can tell
'someone else's anchor' from 'a typo of one of ours'.
LEARNOS Phase 1b emptied the SHARED half of this block. Until
then pw-division, pw-compute and three dash-* were listed here
as well as in `product`, because the guided-tour module pointed
at them too and neither module could rename one alone. That
module and its six tours are gone — ported into `scenarios` in
the content plane — so those five names have exactly one
claimant again and the entries were dropped rather than left as
a claim about a module that is not there.
A SCENARIO STEP MAY POINT AT A FOREIGN ANCHOR, and several do:
pointing is not owning. What the generator requires is that the
name is declared in SOME block of this file, so that a typo is
a build failure rather than a spotlight on nothing.
tests/test_anchor_registry.py enforces every direction:
every product key exists in its template · every pattern prefix is
emitted · every practice key exists in the replica · every anchor the
content names is registered · every data-coach in a scanned file is
declared here or whitelisted as foreign · and the registry never silently
claims an anchor another module owns.

RETIRED (LEARN REFRESH step 1): "retired": true marks a product anchor whose control is gone from its template. The registry keeps the name so content that still points at it is FOUND — tools/check_contract.py lists every use as a WARNING — and test_01 checks the opposite direction: a retired anchor that is back in its template must lose the flag. Delete the entry once no content names it.

ALSO (LEARN REFRESH step 1): "also": [files] lists further templates that draw the SAME control under the same name — the Pay Run hub's Runs board draws pk-kpis / pk-tabs / pk-card as the retired kanban did. test_01 checks every file named.

pw-rail.desc: The four-dot stepper. Where you are in the run, and what is still ahead.

pw-scope.desc: Period and batch name. The two inputs that decide which month is computed.

pw-division.desc: The division / formula configuration. Choosing it chooses the rulebook every payslip in this run is computed by.

pw-summary.desc: Company, configuration and eligible headcount. The last read before anything is computed.

pw-compute.desc: Compute payslips. Creates drafts only — nothing is paid, sent or approved.

pw-result.desc: What the compute produced: the run's name, its net total and its counts.

pw-pills.desc: Payslips / Computed / Need review. The third one is a question, not an error.

pw-exceptions.desc: The exceptions list — every payslip the engine wants a human to look at.

pw-paydata.desc: This month's pay data. The step that only appears when a scheme binds components to spreadsheet columns.

pw-paymode.desc: What should these values do — replace this month only, or update the record?

pw-coverage.desc: Coverage. How many of the people in this run the spreadsheet actually covers.

pw-missing.desc: The people the spreadsheet does not cover, named, with the door that adds them.

pw-skipsheet.desc: Run without a spreadsheet. Skipping is a choice made in front of the list, never a default.

pk-kpis.desc: The numbers row: Pay runs, In pipeline, Awaiting your approval, Completed, Net paid (done) in the company's currency.

pk-run.desc: Run payroll — opens Pay Run › Run.

pk-tabs.desc: The board itself: three columns, Draft · Waiting for approval · Done.

pk-datechips.desc: Date chips on the kanban fallback board (not on the Pay Run hub's Runs tab).

pk-divchips.desc: The division chips above the board. They narrow the cards; the numbers row still counts the whole board.

pk-card.desc: A pay run card. Emitted once per record, so a point-at lands on the first card on the board — enough to say 'a card looks like this', not enough to say 'that one'.

pk-card-actions.desc: A run card's action footer: Submit for approval / Reject on a draft, Open the approval when it is your turn, Pay & Deliver / Report / Excel / Journals / Payments when Done.

ps-runsel.desc: The run selector. Everything below it belongs to the run named here.

ps-kpis.desc: Payslips, net total, gross total, approved and need-review for this run.

ps-chips.desc: Filter chips: All / Need review / HR pending / GM pending / Done.

ps-list.desc: The payslip list. A flag dot marks a slip the engine wants read.

ps-detail.desc: The detail pane for the selected employee.

ps-status.desc: The approval stepper. It is the payslip's own position in the chain, not the run's.

ps-breakdown.desc: Salary breakdown, line by line with its rule code. The working behind the net figure.

im-kpis.desc: Batches, completed, in progress, with errors, connectors.

im-cta.desc: Start an import. Opens the guided wizard — the only path that scores a file before it commits.

im-launches.desc: The secondary launches: the older per-tool import surfaces.

im-pipe.desc: map → validate → commit. A batch that stops before commit has changed nothing.

im-batches.desc: Recent batches and their state. Where you go back to a file that stalled.

iw-steps.desc: The wizard's stepper: source, review & match, validate & fix, commit.

iw-source.desc: Where the data comes from, and which formula configuration reads it.

iw-review.desc: Rows loaded, matched, new and needing attention. The confidence read before any fix.

iw-fixrows.desc: Match / Retry / Skip. Fixing the INPUT here is what stops a wrong payslip later.

iw-outcome.desc: What the commit actually created: employees and payslips.

iw-commit.desc: Commit import. The first irreversible control in this flow — everything before it is a preview.

lg-kpis.desc: The ledger KPI band. ONE template serves Full & Final, Proration Audit and Retro Adjustments, so this key means a different set of numbers on each — the screen key decides which.

lg-facets.desc: The facet chips and the date row. Same control, different facets per ledger.

lg-rows.desc: The ledger rows. Each is a line of working, not a record to edit.

lg-openfull.desc: Open full list. Leaves the cockpit for the underlying list view.

fs-config.desc: The configuration switcher. Its name IS the rulebook a division is paid by — reading it is how you know which config you are editing.

fs-components.desc: The component outline: every named piece of the rulebook, in four kinds. A payslip line exists because a component here produced it.

fs-formula.desc: The formula itself, as coloured chips. Each chip is a component you can click through to; the colour is its kind.

fs-namesletters.desc: Names / Letters. One formula in two spellings — names to explain it, letters to read it beside a spreadsheet.

fs-deps.desc: Depends on / Used by. The blast radius of a rename or a deletion, written down before you make one.

fs-preview.desc: The live preview: the whole configuration evaluated against one sample employee, line by line.

st-new.desc: New insurance policy. A rate change is a NEW RECORD with its own code and effective date; there is no version chain to edit.

st-kpis.desc: Contributions, employee leg, employer leg, policies, tax tables, dependents.

st-rates.desc: The active insurance rates table: scheme, employee share, employer share and ceiling. The near end of L6's trace — the 1.5% that becomes a deduction.

st-effective.desc: The effective date of the policy on display. The field that decides which rates a payslip is computed with, and the whole of the risk in changing one.

st-slabs.desc: The progressive thuế TNCN bands for the active tax year.

st-filters.desc: Insurance policies / tax tables, and the active-only chip. Every count in the roster below is scoped by these.

st-roster.desc: The policy roster. Two rows is the healthy shape: a rate change ends one record and starts another, so the list reads as a history.

sr-new.desc: New structure. Present, and almost always the wrong control: new pay logic belongs in a formula configuration.

sr-kpis.desc: Structures, salary rules, categories, employees covered and countries.

sr-filters.desc: Status, search, date and country chips. They scope the roster, not the database.

sr-roster.desc: The structure cards. Each is history: the rule set a payslip from before the migration was computed by.

sr-openall.desc: Open full structures list. Leaves the cockpit for the underlying list view.

ig-connect.desc: Connect a system. Adds a source payroll data can arrive from without anybody retyping it.

ig-kpis.desc: Connectors, connected, errors, synced records, field mappings and staged records.

ig-filters.desc: Status, search, recency and type chips over the connector roster.

ig-roster.desc: The connector cards, with the last-sync time and the staged count. A connector that stopped still says connected — the sync time is the tell.

st-newpolicy-date.desc: The effective date on the new-policy wizard. It is the company's record of when a rate change legally started — read by auditors and by the statutory reports, and NOT a switch: the cockpit displays the latest-dated active policy the moment it is saved.

dash-hero.desc: The dashboard hero: who you are, which run is live, and how much of it is done. The first sentence Payobook says to anybody who logs in.

dash-kpis.desc: Headcount, monthly payroll, pending approvals and active configurations. Four numbers that describe the company, not the day.

dash-runpayroll.desc: Run Payroll, from the hero. The same wizard the sidebar leaf opens — the dashboard is a way in, never a second way of doing it.

dash-formula.desc: The formula engine card. Payobook computes pay from readable configurations rather than fixed structures, and this is where the dashboard says so.

pe-head.desc: The Employees header and its two actions: Select, which turns on bulk mode, and Add employee. The Add employee button opens the three-step onboarding wizard (pb_people_advanced), which is what the `addperson` intent points at.

pe-bulk.desc: The bulk bar. Visible only in select mode, and the one control on this screen that changes many records at once.

pe-kpis.desc: Headcount, running contracts, contracts expiring within 30 days, new hires this month, the monthly wage bill and the payroll-ready share.

pe-filters.desc: Status chips, search and the date range. Every count above is scoped by whatever is active here.

pe-roster.desc: The employee cards: job, department, wage, contract expiry and the payroll-ready tick. Read the tick before a run, not after it.

ct-head.desc: The Contracts header. A separate screen from Employees on purpose: a person is not a contract, and payroll is paid from the contract.

ct-kpis.desc: Running, expiring within 30 days, draft, expired, the monthly wage bill and the average wage.

ct-filters.desc: Status chips, search and the date range over the contract roster.

ct-roster.desc: The contract cards, each with its period and its wage. The expiry chip is the one to read in the week before a run.

in-hero.desc: The headline figure and the run it was read from. Every number on this board is a door back to where it came from.

in-trend.desc: The cost story over three, six or twelve months. A trend answers a different question from a total, and the window chip decides which.

in-duo.desc: Department leaderboard and the statutory split, side by side: where the cost sits, and how much of it is the law rather than salary.

in-pulse.desc: Workforce pulse — attendance exceptions and headcount movement for this week and month to date.

in-explore.desc: Ask something else. The way out of a board that has answered every question it anticipated, into the Explorer.

ex-head.desc: The Explorer header. A question builder rather than a report: pick a measure, break it down, filter it.

ex-rail.desc: The chip rail: measure, breakdown and comparison. The three choices that define the question being asked.

ex-filters.desc: The Where group — every active filter as a removable tag. A figure read without checking this is a figure read out of scope.

ex-headline.desc: The result headline: the measure, the dimension it is broken down by, and the total the table sums to.

ex-table.desc: The result table. Rows are the breakdown, columns are the comparison — and it reconciles with the payslips it was derived from.

wa-head.desc: The Workforce Insights header. Attendance, overtime, leave and cost per head, read off payroll rather than off a separate HR system.

wa-filters.desc: Division and period pickers. They scope every panel below, which is why an alarming number is worth re-reading with these in view.

wa-kpis.desc: Employees paid, joiners and leavers, and the cost per head. Employees PAID, not employed — the difference is the point.

wa-chart.desc: Headcount paid, month by month. A step in this line is a joiner wave, a leaver wave, or a run that did not include everybody.

wa-duo.desc: Attendance exceptions beside overtime. Two panels because the second is usually the consequence of the first.

gr-head.desc: The filings header, naming the company, its country and the month being filed for. The period control is a month, not a date range.

gr-countries.desc: The country chips. Shown only when this company runs payroll in more than one country, because the filings are the country's, not Payobook's.

gr-grid.desc: The report tiles, grouped by the authority that asks for them. Each opens the existing wizard prefilled with the company and the period.

gr-empty.desc: The honest empty state: this country's filings are not built yet. Better than a tile that generates a form nobody can submit.

helper-orb.desc: The one helper button (LEARN v3), bottom-right on every screen. Opens the Guide / Ask / Practice drawer. Named by scenario sc_welcome's last step; it replaced the PayAI pill, which hides itself when this module is installed.

pw-scheme.desc: The pay-scheme cards, shown when the company has more than one scheme. Choosing one chooses who is paid and in which currency.

dash-period.desc: The one line that says which payroll month every number on the page describes.

ex-trail.desc: Where you are standing in the group, and what one step down would show. Every crumb is a way back.

ex-when.desc: The period picker: the one choice every number on the Explorer depends on.

pk-steps.desc: The numbered steps 01 Draft · 02 Waiting for approval · 03 Done, with their counts and flags (sent back, waiting on you).

pk-route.desc: On a waiting run's card: the step it is at and who it is with.

pk-rejected.desc: The folded Rejected pay runs list under the board.

ai-head.desc: The inbox's action strip: Ask for a sign-off, Workflows, Refresh.

ai-scope.desc: Mine / My team / Everyone — what you can SEE, not what you may decide. Drawn only when there is more than one option.

ai-tabs.desc: The four tabs: My turn · All I can see · Sent back · Finished.

ai-card.desc: One request card: title, badge, who sent it in, Waiting for …, route dots, amount, count, due.

ai-route.desc: A request's route dots: done · current · next.

ai-facts.desc: The facts frozen when the request was sent in (for a pay run: net, gross, payslips, employees, change against the last run, contains overtime).

ai-turndown.desc: Turn it down — ends the request; a pay run is Rejected.

ai-sendback.desc: Send it back — returns it for changes; a pay run is a draft again with the note.

ai-move.desc: Move it to somebody else — for whoever looks after the workflow.

ai-withdraw.desc: Withdraw it — for the person who sent it in; a pay run returns to Draft.

fs-views.desc: The six views: Cards · Grid · Test · Compare · Health · Settings.

fs-command.desc: Tools — the Command Center (Ctrl/Cmd K); Simulate is under Analyze.

bp-status.desc: The guided setup status pill: Not saved yet / Saving… / Draft · saved … / Setup complete / Could not save — retry.

bp-rail.desc: The six-step rail: Start, Pay rules, Connect, Outputs, Test, Finish.

bp-foot.desc: The footer: Step N of 6 · N components, Back, and Continue naming where it goes. The first Continue creates the draft.

bp-pay.desc: "See it in someone's pay": the sample person's estimated take-home pay and its lines (the Scoreboard on the Test step).

bp-identity.desc: Start step, Identity card: company, configuration name, country, pay cycle, effective from.

bp-country.desc: Start step, the Country field and its "Pays in …" money chip.

bp-starters.desc: Start step, "How would you like to start?" starting points.

bp-audience.desc: Start step, "Who are you paying?" tiles.

bp-reallife.desc: Start step, "Real life belongs in the design" checks.

mp-story.desc: Mapping header sentence: FROM a source ══ N ══▶ TO a scheme; both ends are pickers.

mp-modes.desc: Mapping tabs, one per kind of wire; Journey is the cold-start tab.

mp-ramp.desc: Spreadsheet tab, the Excel on-ramp: reads headings and one example row; imports nothing.

mp-jbar.desc: Journey bar: the scheme name and "N need a source · N fed · N not fed yet".

mp-lanes.desc: Journey lanes: Files & systems, Feeds, Transformations, Scheme, Payobook Source.

am-hero.desc: Approval Matrix hero: Bring in from a spreadsheet, Create a workflow.

am-tabs.desc: Approval Matrix tabs: Matrix, People & backups, History.

am-filters.desc: Approval Matrix search and area / status chips.

am-bulk.desc: Approval Matrix bulk bar: No approval needed for all (N).

am-table.desc: Approval Matrix table: Process and the route it follows, Applies to, Status, Version.

am-foot.desc: Approval Matrix footnote: In use only when published and wired; No approval needed is still recorded.

rd-head.desc: Records Desk header: subtitle, scheme pill, File, History, Review N changes.

rd-scheme.desc: Records Desk scheme pill: the scheme and how many fields it maps.

rd-file.desc: Records Desk file doors: Export with data, Export blank template, Import a file.

rd-history.desc: Records Desk History: every apply, with an Undo.

rd-review.desc: Records Desk Review N changes button.

rd-who.desc: Records Desk Who rail: search and facets.

rd-fields.desc: Records Desk Fields strip: the columns on the grid.

rd-empty.desc: Records Desk empty state when the scheme maps no fields: Open Mapping.

gp-head.desc: Group page header: Your group, History, Edit the group.

gp-tree.desc: Group tree: the group, its currency and rate policy, and each company with its currency and pay schemes.

gp-rates.desc: Exchange rates card: How rates are picked and the 12-month coverage strip.

gp-divisions.desc: Divisions card: parts of the business across companies.

ex-money.desc: Explorer money switch: the shown currency, and Group currency / Each in its own money.

tr-head.desc: Component treatment header: Re-classify from the formulas, Save N change(s).

tr-filters.desc: Component treatment chips: All, Needs your answer, Stored differently, Type says otherwise.

tr-table.desc: Component treatment table: Component, Comes from, Group, Pay role, Subtotal, Tells the run, Value type.

pp-tabs.desc: People › Pay's own tabs: Bands, Fairness, Review, Changes.

pp-bands-tools.desc: Bands header: Work it out again, Export, Import, Place a new hire.

pp-band-picture.desc: The band picture: each band's range and middle, a dot per person; Dense rows, Fit to this family.

pp-health.desc: Worth knowing: below / above the band, newer people paid more, a manager paid less, band width.

pp-fairness.desc: Fairness: pay gap by gender across everybody, then by level, team and job.

pp-reviews.desc: Pay reviews card: Set up guidance, New review.

pp-meters.desc: An open review's meters: Budget, Fairness, Scores.

pp-stepper.desc: An open review's stepper: Being written → With HR → With finance → With the CEO → Approved → Applied.

pp-review-actions.desc: An open review's action bar: Send for approval, Approve for HR/finance, Approve it, Apply, Take it back, Send back.

pp-stops.desc: What stops approval (only with a blocker).

pp-worksheet.desc: The worksheet: filters and the Person … A year columns.

pp-bulk.desc: Worksheet tools: Use the guidance, Add 1%, Take off 1%, Share out what is left, Paste scores, Calibration.

pp-calibration.desc: Calibration marks: in line with the others, stands out, breaks a limit.

pp-second-look.desc: Calibration's Worth a second look list.

pp-changes.desc: Changes tab: Pay changes, New pay change.

dr-head.desc: Decision Room header: See the year before you commit to it; Undo, Reset, Save plan.

dr-levers.desc: Shape your plan: What if we… and the levers.

dr-presets.desc: Presets: Grow thoughtfully, Invest in people, Ease overtime.

dr-goals.desc: Your definition of a good year: the goal compass.

dr-results.desc: Result tabs: Work & shifts, Why profit changed, People & pay, Room to hire.

dr-compare.desc: Compare possibilities, with confidence: the saved plans table.

dr-propose.desc: A saved plan's verbs: Propose, Approve, Send back, Keep editing a copy (first row).

dr-exact.desc: A saved plan's Exact cost (first row).

hi-steps.desc: The four-step strip: Request & approve … Welcome aboard.

hi-row.desc: The role cards, each with Step X of 4 — or, when the board has nobody on it, its empty-board message (both carry the anchor; one renders at a time).

hi-next.desc: A role card's Next: line (first card).

hi-wizard.desc: The request wizard: Let's shape your next hire.

nj-steps.desc: Getting ready → Settling in → Checklist done.

nj-list.desc: The joiner cards — or, when the board has nobody on it, its empty-board message (both carry the anchor; one renders at a time).

nj-drawer.desc: The joiner drawer: Still to do, Done, Conversations.

nj-buddy.desc: The drawer's people strip: HR contact, Buddy, Their record.

ex2-steps.desc: Working their notice → Signing off → Ready to settle → Settled.

ex2-list.desc: The leaver cards — or, when the board has nobody on it, its empty-board message (both carry the anchor; one renders at a time).

ex2-clearance.desc: A card's Signed off by lights: IT, HR, Finance, Admin (first card).

ex2-settle.desc: The settlement block: Close settlement, Open the settlement.

pr-list.desc: The trial cards — or, when the board has nobody on it, its empty-board message (both carry the anchor; one renders at a time).

pr-verdict.desc: Confirm them / Extend the trial / Do not confirm (Decide wizard).

gw-list.desc: The plan cards — or, when the board has nobody on it, its empty-board message (both carry the anchor; one renders at a time).

gw-objectives.desc: What has to change: objectives on track / at risk / met / not met.

cl-steps.desc: Running → Decision needed → Being agreed → Decided.

cl-list.desc: The contract cards — or, when the board has nobody on it, its empty-board message (both carry the anchor; one renders at a time).

cl-decide.desc: Make it permanent / Extend it / Let it end.

wf-needs.desc: The Needs you panel (My team / Organisation).

wf-clean.desc: Approve all N clean (only with clean overtime).

wf-time.desc: Time's tabs: Timeline, Week Grid, Exceptions, Import.

wf-timeoff.desc: Time Off head: month and Apply on behalf.

wf-outtoday.desc: Out today (only when someone is out).

wf-close.desc: Close head: the week and N flagged.

wf-close-flags.desc: The flags table: Fix, Approve as-is, Review all.

wf-close-handoff.desc: Payroll handoff: Regular hours, Overtime, Bonus hours, Est. gross.

cp-generate.desc: Generate a filing: the flow page.

cp-bank-steps.desc: Draft → HR Review → Finance Review → Approved.

cp-audit-filters.desc: Audit filters: Today, This week, By me, Salary only, Logins.

pp-tab-.desc: One per People › Pay tab: pp-tab-bands, pp-tab-fairness, pp-tab-review, pp-tab-changes (t-attf-data-coach). A walkthrough presses Review to open that tab — switching a tab reads, it writes nothing.

practice.rep-nav: The replica's own sidebar. Mirrors pb_sidebar; nothing on it navigates the real app.
practice.rep-banner: The practice banner. Says, on every screen, that none of this is your company.
practice.rep-pipeline: The pay run's road on the Runs replica: Draft → Waiting for approval → Done, with the two ways off it (sent back, turned down). A teaching view; the product draws this as columns and a route line.
practice.rep-tabs: The replica's tab strip for the page being shown. Mirrors the product's hub tabs, in their order and words; tabs with no practice screen are drawn quiet and say so.
practice.rep-fs-stage: The practice Formula Studio's stage badge and the Draft → Testing → Validated → Active chain drawn beside it. The product has the badge; the drawn chain is a teaching view.
practice.rep-fs-tools: The practice panel that stands for Tools → Analyze → Simulate. In the product it is the Command Center overlay (fs-command opens it); here it is drawn open so a lesson can point at Simulate.
practice.rep-settings: The practice company's Settings page of categories. The product draws the same categories; only the four with practice screens open anything here.
practice.rep-impfix: The import wizard's one repairable cell — the overtime amount on the row whose figure could not be read. A real input; the value a learner types is checked loosely against the step's own value, thousands marks and all.
practice.rep-impmatch: The Match button on that same row. Practice-only because the product's importer offers its fixes differently; here it is what 'accept this row' looks like.
practice.rep-newemp-open: The Add employee button on the Employees replica. In the product it opens a form view; here it is the step that takes the learner down to the practice form.
practice.rep-newemp-name: The practice employee form's name field. A real input, declared in INPUT_ANCHORS as text, so tone marks are optional when it is checked.
practice.rep-newemp-div: The practice employee form's division picker. A click target, not an input: choosing the division is choosing which formula configuration will pay this person.
practice.rep-newemp-save: The practice employee form's Save button. It saves nothing — there is no server behind the replica — and the step that presses it is guarded for the same reason the real one would be.
practice.rep-watermark: The practice-mode watermark. Says on every free-roam screen that none of this is real. Drawn unconditionally by the practice view builder; no product screen has one.
practice.rep-bp-rules: The guided setup's Pay rules list on the practice company, each component as a sentence with its formula.
practice.rep-bp-added: The component being added in the Pay rules replica (Allowances). The lesson's tick moment happens beside it.
practice.rep-bp-paynum: The practice pay panel's take-home figure. Carries data-from / data-to so the tick moment can count from the before to the after value; the product shows the same number without the count.
practice.rep-jny-file: The HR system's basic_salary field on the practice Journey — where Mai's base salary starts.
practice.rep-jny-feed: The feed row that carries basic_salary on the practice Journey.
practice.rep-jny-xform: The practice Journey's transformation card (text to amount).
practice.rep-jny-scheme: LCB on the practice Journey's Scheme lane — where the value is fed.
practice.rep-jny-slip: Mai's Base salary payslip line, drawn beside the practice Journey so the whole road fits on one screen. The product shows the payslip elsewhere.
practice.rep-jny-source: The practice Journey's Payobook Source card, with Open Records Desk.
practice.rep-mp-runlane: The From this pay run group on the practice spreadsheet tab.
practice.rep-mp-conflict: The source-conflict question on the practice spreadsheet tab, drawn open. In the product it is a dialog that appears when a second source is wired.
practice.rep-ct-warn: The Type says otherwise warning line on the practice Component treatment board.
practice.rep-am-payrow: The pay run row of the practice Approval Matrix.
practice.rep-am-bsteps: The practice route builder's five steps: Purpose, People, Safeguards, Review, Publish.
practice.rep-am-route: The practice route builder's steps and the kinds of step it offers.
practice.rep-am-guards: The practice route builder's safeguards and Try an example.
practice.rep-am-publish: The practice route builder's Publish panel, with the date new requests follow it from.
practice.rep-rd-grid: The practice Records Desk grid, with three edited cells.
practice.rep-rd-reviewpanel: The practice Records Desk review drawer, drawn open beside the grid.
practice.rep-gp-foot: The practice Group page's line that nothing is stored in the group currency.
practice.rep-ex-compare: The practice Explorer's Compare schemes panel, each scheme in its own money.
practice.rep-slipline: The worked example's statutory deductions, drawn on the STATUTORY replica beside the rates that produced them. It is the far end of L6's trace and it exists only here: the product's statutory cockpit shows rates, and a payslip shows đồng, and no single product screen shows both at once. Naming it rep- is the honest consequence — the Coach must never claim to point at this on a live screen.
practice.rep-pr-budget: The practice pay review's Budget meter, carrying its before/after for the `meter` moment: it fills as the rises go in.
practice.rep-pr-guide: The practice worksheet's Use the guidance button (a Try target; it changes nothing).
practice.rep-pr-cal: The practice worksheet's Calibration button (a Try target).
practice.rep-pr-send: The practice review's Send for approval button — guarded in Try, like every control that would write.
practice.rep-dr-exact: The practice Decision Room's line comparing the exact cost with the estimate.
practice.rep-hi-cands: The practice Hiring board's candidate strip for the first role, with Nam at Discussion 1.
practice.rep-hi-route: The practice hiring request's sign-off route: manager, HR lead, Finance only if over budget.
practice.rep-hi-send: The practice hiring request's Send for approval — guarded in Try.
practice.rep-ex-card: The practice Exits board's leaver card (Bùi Thị Hạnh), a Try target that opens her drawer.
practice.rep-ex-open: The practice leaver drawer's Open the settlement button.
practice.rep-ex-desks: The practice leaver drawer, drawn open: what each of the four desks checks, and which has not signed.
practice.rep-wf-exc: The practice Time panel's line on exceptions becoming flags on Close.
practice.rep-wf-flag: The practice Close board's first flag row (Hùng's missing check-out).
practice.rep-wf-fix: The Fix button on that flag — the Try step that corrects the day.
practice.rep-wf-asis: The Approve as-is button on that flag row.
practice.rep-wf-locked: The practice Close board's picture of a locked week, with the Reopen… note. Drawn beside the grey lock so the lesson can show both states.
practice.rep-ac-handover: The practice Hand my access over dialog, drawn open: who, what, until, and the automatic take-back.
practice.rep-pm-wall: The practice Wall card: one piece of praise tied to a company value, and Say thank you.
practice.rep-pm-tiles: The practice tiles for People's smaller tabs: Where they work, Assets, Goals, Announce.

foreign.im-connectors: pb_import — the "Manage connectors" deep link the IA redesign's Cycle 3 left behind when it closed Import's five duplicate connector doors. pb_learn neither laid it nor teaches it; the im-* family in that template is otherwise pb_learn's, which is exactly why it has to be named rather than wildcarded.
foreign.ig-data: pb_integrations — the in-cockpit Data section (field mappings, data store, transformation rules) that replaced three raw list views in Cycle 3. Same shape as im-connectors: a new sibling in a family pb_learn owns, laid by somebody else.
foreign.st-data: pb_statutory — the in-cockpit Data section that replaced four legacy VN list tiles in Cycle 4. Same shape again.
foreign.payai-pill: pb_payroll_ai_insights — the PayAI launcher. Named by scenario sc_welcome's last step.
foreign.fs-*: pb_formula_studio — the Formula Studio anchor family, laid in studio.xml by that module. EIGHT are PROMOTED into `product` above (fs-config, fs-components, fs-formula, fs-namesletters, fs-deps, fs-preview, fs-views, fs-command) because L5 names them and an anchor a lesson points at has to be one a test can check; they are listed in PROMOTED_FROM_WILDCARD in tests/test_anchor_registry.py, which is what stops the wildcard reading them as somebody else's. Everything else matching fs-* is still pb_formula_studio's alone — sc_formula points at fs-arrows, fs-card, fs-add, fs-views, fs-view-grid, fs-flow, fs-editai and fs-payai without claiming any of them, which is exactly what this wildcard is for.
foreign.grid-*: pb_formula_studio — the spreadsheet grid. sc_formula points at grid-canvas, grid-fbar and grid-hint; the names belong to that module.
foreign.imp-*: pb_hr_payroll_formula — the multi-sheet import wizard. sc_import points at imp-confidence and imp-actions.
foreign.map-*: pb_hr_payroll_formula — the component-mapping wizard. sc_mapping points at map-intro and map-actions.
